why: TensorFold's OpenAI-compatible server, 'tensorfold serve', run from a recipe's image across the nodes of a cluster. Every rank runs the same command against the checkpoint's local snapshot, and rank 0 also takes the served name, host and port, which is what answers the API. It reads only the Hugging Face cache mounted from each node (HF_HUB_OFFLINE in the recipe), so the pinned models must be downloaded on every node before a launch, and a launch checks they are. Compiled kernels are kept per image patch set, since a kernel built for one set does not fit another, and the spill directory holds kept prompt states across restarts. It checks no API key: its host defaults to 127.0.0.1, and listening wider means fronting it with a proxy that checks one. /v1/models answers only once the model is loaded, which is what upstream's launcher waits for too.

params.name: tensor_parallel
params.why: --tp: how many GPUs the model is split over, across every node. One GPU a node, as on a DGX Spark, makes it the node count.

params.name: bind_host
params.why: --host on rank 0. TensorFold checks no API key, so the default keeps the endpoint on loopback; set it wider only behind a proxy that checks one.

params.name: kernel_cache
params.why: The host directory, under home, mounted at /cache for compiled CUDA kernels. A recipe names one per image patch set, so a different image never loads kernels built for another.

params.name: spill_dir
params.why: The host directory, under home, mounted at /spill, where --snapshot-dir /spill keeps prompt states on disk across restarts.
